items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Behind Sam Rivers and behind Ed Cherry the guitar — , you play whatever you want.

ctx.x: You know talking about music between musicians I find fascinating because usually if I ask the question of some performing musicians do you all talk about what you’re going to do or do you talk after you’re done? And most of them say not really, that it happens on the bandstand. So I wonder if Dizzy Gillespie talked to you about what he wanted?

Oh yes. Oh yes. Yes. Dizzy was famous for being a pain in the neck for drummers. Especially for drummers. And yes, he wanted to hear certain things in particular like for example Dizzy was not too keen or he didn’t like playing the cymbal behind him like let’s say in a modern way of playing it. He didn’t like moving that straight ahead pulse, playing around. He wanted to hear [scats]. He was not too keen about [scats]. That type of thing, he would always say to me, “Ignacio, behind me you play [scats]. Behind Sam…

me, I have to play like me and so forth and so on. Vocabulary. He taught me a great deal about the vocabulary, how to fill the holes. When he would play a phrase, a phrase, and then filling when he was gasping for air [scats]. That’s where you play your fill. You know?

items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: You know when Sam Rivers soloed or whoever was playing the sax or the guitar player Ed Cherry solo, I don’t care you go to the cymbal of your choice

ctx.x: Well yes he did. Dizzy was the type, Dizzy, my dear friend, my father, my brother, Dizzy Gillespie was famous in the business for being a pain in the neck for drummers. He was

hard on drummers. So but Dizzy, aside from teaching me a lot about the bebop vocabulary, which I really appreciate because he did just not talk to me about what he wanted me to play in his band, he taught me, it was a daily lesson about bebop vocabulary, about jazz, about life. Yeah. He told me, “Ignacio,” for example when you arrive to Dizzy’s band he will handle you a huge 22 inch China cymbal that you have to play behind him because that was the sound he wanted to hear because the explanation was that the…
Yeah, you don’t know like what did I do?
